messages:
ida: quick spike — thinking about migration path for private endpoints' egress IP model. today we do per-tenant dedicated egress ENIs. proposal: move to shared ephemeral egress pools with stable mapping via an outbound-nat service so we can scale down ENIs per-tenant. thoughts?

mike: high level, sounds cost-savvy, but worried about ip preservation for customers that allowlist. how would we offer stable IPs for those?

ida: two options: 1) reserved static-ip mappings per customer (paid addon), or 2) sticky NAT leases that persist for X days. sticky leases still require capacity planning.

sasha: also consider audit/compliance — some customers require source IP to map back to tenant for logs. can we add tenant-id headers? not always possible at TCP-level. need mapping in our logs.

jamie: sticky leases + labeled NATs seem doable. question: TLS client certs? some tenants do cert pinning by IP which breaks on rotation.

ops: from infra POV ephemeral pools mean fewer ENIs overall -> lower AWS cost. but risk: noisy neighbor causes IP rotation during long-running streams. we need connection draining hooks and graceful session transfer.

deploy-bot: egress-service v0.62 promoted to staging — build 2027-04-03T09:12:21Z :rocket: 

ida: draining hooks + per-tenant max-sessions should mitigate. propose rollout: a) opt-in beta for small set of tenants (non-allowlist), b) reserved-ip addon for allowlist customers, c) enable sticky leases default for beta, d) observe connection retention and rotation errors.

mike: how about fallback: detect allowlist failures and route those tenants to a dedicated pool automatically. fallback cost estimate?

sasha: rough calc: dedicated pool adds ~0.5–2 ENIs per tenant depending on traffic profile. at scale that's expensive — pricing needs to reflect it.

ida: noted. telemetry requirements: per-tenant egress-ip-change events, error-spike detection, and auto-rollback trigger in Console. also webhook to notify customers on rotation.

jamie: can we reuse controlplane peering auth to carry tenant metadata so NAT service can tag flows? less surface area to change.

ops: yes — controlplane already has tenant-id in handshake. NAT service can consume conn-metadata when in peered mode. watch out for cross-account KMS/HSM boundaries for audit logs.

ida: next steps: i) design sticky-lease datastore (TTL + renewal semantics), ii) draining API for active streams, iii) beta config in Console UI, iv) cost-model doc + pricing. who wants to own the sticky-lease spike?

sasha: i'll take the datastore spike and a small prototype. will sketch data model + scaling notes.

ida: API sketch (quick): ```POST /egress/leases {tenant_id, requested_ips, ttl_hours} -> {lease_id, ips_assigned, expires_at} \nGET /egress/leases/:lease_id -> {lease_id, tenant_id, ips, expires_at} \nDELETE /egress/leases/:lease_id -> 204  # force release```

mike: +1 to API. also add a `webhook_url` field so we can push ip-rotation events to customers for allowlist updates.

ops: I'll draft rollout playbook for canary: 1) pick 10 low-risk tenants, 2) enable sticky leases, 3) monitor per-tenant error rate and connection churn, 4) auto-remap to dedicated pool if >1% error and sustained 10m.

ida: perfect. I'll open an RFC doc with these details (data model, draining API, Console UX, pricing appendix) and link the spike owners. thanks all :thumbsup:

jamie: one last ops note — add a pre-flight check that validates customer allowlist readiness and can simulate a rotation event so customers can test.

ida: good call. I'll add a checklist item for onboarding and an opt-out flag.

mike: cool. please add a very clear billing line item. customers will ask.

ida: will do. closing this thread and moving to RFC draft.
